# Commands — which one, when, and every script's `--help`

<!-- GENERATED by bin/gen-commands-doc.py from the scripts' own `usage:` headers; do not edit. Regenerate: python3 bin/gen-commands-doc.py (bin/check.sh §13 fails when stale). -->

Every script in `~/.local/bin`, `bin/`, `system/` and `install/` answers `-h` / `--help` with the block shown below (exit 0) and prints a one-line usage with exit 2 on a bad argument. `dram <command> --help` works for every subcommand. The first section says which command to reach for; the rest is the scripts' own text.

## Which command when

### Update

| you want | run | and know |
|---|---|---|
| update everything | `dram update` | **canonical.** keyring → `paccache` → `pacman -Syu` (official repos + `[dram]`) → `flatpak update` → pacnew / orphans / reboot report → `dram switch` → `dram doctor --brief` |
| the same, old spelling | `sysupdate` | a shim: `exec dram update "$@"`, flags pass through |
| the monthly one with cleanup | `upgrade` | a bash alias for `dram update --clean` (`modules/shell.nix`): **interactive shells only** — scripts and `ssh host upgrade` call `dram` directly |
| see what is pending, change nothing | `dram update --check` | read-only: `checkupdates` (official + `[dram]`), `arch-audit -u`, then a build (not a switch) of the dram |
| also bump the pinned nix inputs | `dram update --full` | `nix flake update`; `flake.lock` is restored if the rebuilt dram fails to switch |
| also expire old generations and collect garbage | `dram update --clean` | Home Manager generations older than 7 days + `nix-collect-garbage` |
| update but leave the flake alone | `dram update --no-switch` | everything except the final `dram switch` |
| only packages, by hand | `sudo pacman -Syu` | lower level: no keyring check, no pacnew report, no switch, no doctor — `dram update` wraps these |
| only Flatpaks | `flatpak update` | lower level; `dram update` runs it |
| apply the flake after editing `modules/` | `dram switch` (= `dram-switch`) | the flake for `pj@<host>` with a dated `-b bak-<stamp>`. Bare `home-manager switch` is **forbidden**: it ignores the flake and once tore down every dotfile symlink |
| go back one Home Manager generation | `dram rollback [N]` | asks first; `dram switch` goes forward again |
| take a vendored package to its new AUR version | `dram pkgs update <name>` | **packaging, not updating**: edits `pkgs/<name>` on cabin; then `dram pkgs build`, `dram pkgs publish`, `bin/sync-dram-repo.sh`, and `dram update` installs it |
| converge `/etc`, hooks, timers, services | `sudo bash system/maintenance.sh` | **convergence, not updating**: idempotent, `--dry-run` first |
| get this repo's commits onto a host | `bin/push-host.sh pj@<host>` (Mac) | deploys the repo (tracked files only) plus every tag; `~/.local/bin` is symlinked into it, so scripts are live at once; `dram switch` on the host only when `modules/` changed. A host detached at a release (channel stable) keeps its checkout until `dram update` |
| get a release onto a Windows PC | `bin/push-windows.sh <host> [--apply]` (Mac) | the flake's render and every file its manifest lists, only what changed since the PC's live release; `dram receive` there checks each sha256 and switches `C:\ProgramData\dram`, `--apply` converges, `--dry-run` changes nothing on Windows (`docs/operations/releases/pushes.md`) |

### Release

| you want | run | and know |
|---|---|---|
| see what version a host runs | `dram version` | from `~/.config/dram/release`, written by `dram switch`: release tag (or `0.0.0-dev`), build id `<date>.<sha>`, channel, Home Manager generation; `--json` for scripts |
| know if a newer build is out | `dram update --check` | `dram: <current> -> <target> (N commits)` or `dram: up to date`; **exit 7 when nothing at all is pending** (packages, Flatpaks, dram) — the SteamOS convention. The welcome toast and the bar badge say the same |
| follow releases or the newest push | `dram channel stable` / `dram channel main` | **stable** = the latest `v*` tag, **main** = `master` as pushed from the Mac; `dram update` checks the target out before it touches packages. Default: stable once a tag exists |
| read the release notes | `dram changelog [vX | --since vX]` | the matching sections of `CHANGELOG.md` |
| cut a release | `bin/release.sh -m "<summary>"` (Mac) | clean tree + `check.sh` green → next `vYYYY.MM.N` → `CHANGELOG.md` section → annotated tag → `push-host.sh` to every host with `dram.address`; `--dry-run` shows it all, `--checkpoint` marks a build every host must pass through |
| go back to the previous build | `dram rollback` | checks out the previous build's commit, activates its Home Manager generation, **prints** (never runs) the `sudo pacman -U /var/cache/pacman/pkg/…` lines for packages that differ; `dram rollback --list` = `dram builds` shows the last 5 recorded builds |

### Theme

| you want | run | and know |
|---|---|---|
| switch the theme | `dram theme [name]` (= `dram-theme`) | without a name: the rofi picker (**SUPER+T**); a name is the bar name or the dir id; `dram theme --list` shows both |
| follow the sun | `dram-theme-auto` | the systemd user timer runs it **every 10 min** and at login; it only flips `washi` ↔ `washi-day` and the night light, and never overrides a theme picked by hand; `--print` shows the times |
| night light now | `nightlight.sh` | **SUPER+ALT+N**; hands control back to the sun on the second press |
| another wallpaper on this monitor | `wallpaper-menu.sh` | **SUPER+SHIFT+W**; `quote-wallpaper.sh` repaints the quote wall on the next theme switch or hotplug |
| re-render the quote wallpaper | `quote-wallpaper.sh [--en|--ru|--show]` | run at login, by `dram-theme` and by `wallpaper-hotplug.sh`; a theme's `wall.sh` overrides it |
| regenerate a theme's adapter files after editing its palette | `bin/gen-*.py [theme]` | **dev-time, on the Mac**: rofi, GTK, browser, kitty tabs, TUI, VS Code, yazi; commit the output — `dram-theme` only links files |

### Lock

| you want | run | and know |
|---|---|---|
| lock now | **SUPER+L** | `pidof hyprlock || hyprlock` (hyprland.lua); no script |
| the power menu | **SUPER+X** / **SUPER+M** | `power-menu.sh` (a rofi list): lock, logout, suspend, reboot, shutdown |
| automatic | `hypridle` | **30 min** → lock (`loginctl lock-session`; + suspend on battery) · **45 min** → screens off (`dotfiles/.config/hypr/hypridle.conf`) |
| the lid | `lid.sh open|close` | disables / re-enables the internal panel while docked; it **does not lock** (hypridle's `before_sleep_cmd` does, on suspend) |

### Back up

| you want | run | and know |
|---|---|---|
| automatic | borgmatic user timer | **03:00** daily (+ up to 1 h jitter) to the peer host (`modules/backup.nix`, `docs/operations/backups/README.md`) |
| a backup now | `dram backup` (= `backup` alias) | `borgmatic --verbosity 1` |
| see or verify what is there | `dram backup list`, `dram backup check` | borgmatic list / check |
| a file back | `dram backup restore ~/path` | from the latest archive into `/tmp/dram-restore/`; copy it back yourself |
| the third copy on the Mac | `bin/pull-backups.sh` | launchd daily **06:00** + at login (`install/mac-launchd.sh`); stages each host's repo under the Borg lock, rsyncs it into `~/backups/borg/on-<host>/`; `--check` prints the copies' age |
| an offline copy on the eva drive | `backup-eva` alias | `system/backup-eva.sh`, by hand when the drive is plugged in |

### Health

| you want | run | and know |
|---|---|---|
| the host | `dram doctor` | read-only; every warning names its fix; `--brief` warnings only, `--boot` adds the boot chain, `--supply` provenance only |
| the repo | `dram check` | `bin/check.sh` (nix-free invariants, runs on the Mac too) then `nix flake check` where nix exists |
| pending updates | `dram update --check` | see Update |
| the `[dram]` package repo | `dram pkgs check` | manifest, pins, no shadowing; `bin/check.sh` §12 runs it |
| reproducibility | `bin/repro.sh` | archlinux-repro for the official set, double build + diffoscope for ours (`docs/security/software-supply/integrity.md`) |
| what a system script would do | `--dry-run` | every writer in `system/` and `install/bootstrap.sh` take it and need no root for it |

## `~/.local/bin` — on every host

Linked into `~/.local/bin`: `dram` and its two shims by `modules/cli.nix` on every host, the rest by `modules/desktop.nix` (the desktop's own commands).

### `codium-themes-install`

invoked by: `dram-theme`, on every switch

```
usage: codium-themes-install [--marketplace]

Makes the editor's dram themes available: registers the local Letterpress
extension (dotfiles/.vscode/extensions/letterpress-themes, one generated VS
Code theme per dram theme, bin/gen-vscode-themes.py) in
~/.vscode/extensions/extensions.json, and with --marketplace also installs
the pinned historical marketplace themes. Works for VS Code (~/.vscode) and
VSCodium (~/.vscode-oss); the name is historical. Needs no editor binary for
the default. Idempotent; dram-theme runs it on every switch.

  --marketplace   also install the pinned marketplace themes (id@version)
  -h, --help      this text

exit: 0 ok · 1 an install failed · 2 bad usage
see: dotfiles/.vscode/extensions/letterpress-themes/README.md
```

### `dram`

invoked by: by hand; the bar's updates badge click (`kitty -e dram update`); `dram-switch`, `sysupdate`, the `upgrade` alias

```
usage: dram <command> [args]

Updates, applies, themes and checks this host: the Home Manager flake for
<user>@<host> (host from /etc/hostname), the Arch update path, the theme, health
and backups, and the [dram] package repo. Every command answers --help.

  switch                  apply the Home Manager flake for <user>@<host> (never bare home-manager);
                          writes ~/.config/dram/release (the running build's identity)
  update [--check] [--full] [--clean] [--no-switch]
                          record the build -> check out the channel target -> keyring ->
                          paccache -> pacman -Syu -> flatpak -> pacnew -> orphans ->
                          reboot? -> switch -> doctor --brief; --check exits 7 when nothing is pending;
                          in a WSL clone it first receives a newer staged bundle
  receive [<bundle>] [--force]
                          take the branch and tags from a git bundle without ssh (a WSL clone:
                          the one bin/push-host.sh --wsl staged in C:\ProgramData\dram)
  version [--json]        the running build: version, build id, channel, generation
  channel [stable|main|--target]
                          what `dram update` follows: stable = latest release tag, main = master
  changelog [vX|--since vX]
                          release notes from CHANGELOG.md (latest section by default)
  theme [name|--list|--ids]
                          switch the desktop theme (dram-theme); --list = bar name + id, --ids = ids
  check                   repo invariants (bin/check.sh) + nix flake check
  doctor [--boot] [--brief] [--supply]
                          read-only health report; every warning names its fix
                          (--supply: provenance and integrity only)
  pacnew                  merge *.pacnew with vim -d (pacdiff -s)
  rollback [N|--list|--system [N]]
                          no args: the previous build (commit + generation; pacman -U lines printed);
                          N: the Nth previous Home Manager generation; --list: recorded builds;
                          --system: the snapper snapshots, --system N: restore one as / (decisions/0011)
  builds                  = rollback --list
  backup [run|list|check|restore <path>]
                          borgmatic to the peer host; restore lands in /tmp/dram-restore
  apply [--dry-run] [--prune] [--yes] [--rollout]
                          converge the system layer to this host's roles: declared packages,
                          units, role hooks; reports what no role declares (decisions/0008)
  harvest                 refresh hosts/<host>/ (packages, units, /etc copies) from this box
  boot-to <os|list>       reboot once into another OS on this machine (firmware BootNext):
                          windows, debian, fedora, nixos, or an entry number; list shows them
  pkgs <check|update|build|publish|log|list>
                          the [dram] package repo (bin/pkgs.sh)
  yubikey <status|enroll|ssh|use>
                          the YubiKeys: enrol one, fetch its SSH handle on this host, choose
                          the key that signs (bin/yubikey.sh, docs/security/identity/yubikeys.md)
  help, -h, --help        this text

Shims kept for muscle memory: sysupdate = dram update, upgrade = dram update
--clean (interactive shells only), dram-switch = dram switch. On a host set up
before 2026-10-06 the first dram command moves the old rice state directories
(~/.config/rice, ~/.local/state/rice, ~/.cache/rice{,-pkgs}) to their dram names,
file by file, once (decisions/0007).

needs:  bash, git, nix and home-manager, pacman and pacman-contrib; by command
        flatpak, borgmatic, snapper, efibootmgr, sbctl; this repo at ~/git/dotfiles
        (DRAM_REPO overrides it)
alone:  no: it reads the host files, packages/, system/*.tsv and install/lib/;
        dram-switch and sysupdate are one-line shims onto it
here:   linked into ~/.local/bin by modules/cli.nix on every host; bin/check.sh
        §13 runs each subcommand's --help and a bad flag in a throwaway clone
exit:   0 ok · 1 the command failed · 2 bad usage · 7 `update --check`: nothing pending
see:    docs/operations/dram/README.md, docs/operations/releases/README.md
```

### `dram-theme`

invoked by: **SUPER + T** — theme switcher; `dram theme`; `dram-theme-auto`

```
usage: dram-theme [name|--list|--ids]

Switches the whole desktop between colour themes. ~/.config/themes/<name>/
holds per-app adapter files (waybar.css, kitty.conf, rofi.rasi, ...); apps
include the stable path ~/.config/themes/current/..., and this repoints that
one symlink, patches the few apps without include support (sed) and fires the
reloads. Nothing leaves $HOME (the boot chain and ly are untouched). A name
is the bar name (MENU_NAME in meta.sh) or the directory id; without one, the
rofi picker (SUPER+T). `dram theme` is the same command.

  --list        bar name and id of every theme
  --ids         directory ids only (completion)
  -h, --help    this text

exit: 0 ok (or picker cancelled) · 1 no such theme or a step failed · 2 bad usage
see: docs/design/themes/switcher.md
```

### `dram-theme-auto`

invoked by: systemd user timer every 10 min + at login (`modules/desktop.nix`); `nightlight.sh` (with `--nightlight`)

```
usage: dram-theme-auto [--print|-n|--dry-run] [--nightlight]

Follows the sun between the two washi themes (washi-day between sunrise and sunset, washi otherwise) and drives the hyprsunset night light the same way (identity by day, warm after sunset). Only ever switches when the current theme is one of those two, so a theme picked by hand (SUPER+T) is never overridden; a no-op when already right. Run by the systemd user timer every 10 minutes (modules/desktop.nix) and at login. Location: ~/.config/dram/location, one line "LAT LON" (decimal degrees, east positive; dram.location writes it); sunrise/sunset come from the NOAA solar-position approximation (+-2 min), pure Python.

  --print, -n, --dry-run   show today's times and what would happen; change nothing
  --nightlight             re-apply only the night light's sun state (nightlight.sh's "off" press)
  -h, --help               this text

exit: 0 ok · 1 the wanted theme is not installed or dram-theme failed · 2 bad usage
see: docs/design/themes/switcher.md
```

### `kb-layout.sh`

invoked by: **SUPER + ALT + SPACE** — keyboard layout en/ru; **ALT + SHIFT_L** — keyboard layout en/ru (Alt+Shift); **SHIFT + ALT_L** — keyboard layout en/ru (Shift+Alt); bar: `hyprland/language` (on-click)

```
usage: kb-layout.sh [toggle|en|ru|status]

Keeps every keyboard on the same layout. Hyprland lists the lid switch, power
button and video bus as "keyboards" and toggles layouts per device, so they
drift apart; this sets all of them to one explicit index with
`hyprctl switchxkblayout all N`. Default action: toggle (SUPER+ALT+SPACE,
Alt+Shift, the bar's layout click).

  toggle        next layout on every keyboard (default)
  en, ru        that layout on every keyboard
  status        print the main keyboard's layout (us / ru); needs the
                desktop's Hyprland socket (a terminal on the host, not ssh)
  -h, --help    this text

exit: 0 ok · 1 hyprctl failed · 2 bad usage
see: docs/design/shell-and-bars/keybinds.md
```

### `keybind-cheatsheet.sh`

invoked by: **SUPER + slash** — keybind cheatsheet

```
usage: keybind-cheatsheet.sh [--markdown]

Searchable keybind cheatsheet (SUPER+/): parses the hl.bind() lines straight
out of ~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua, so it never goes stale, and shows them in
rofi. A bind's description (or trailing -- comment) is its text. With
--markdown it prints docs/design/shell-and-bars/keybinds.md to stdout
instead; the committed file is generated by that call, so regenerate it after
touching a bind (the exact command is printed at the top of the doc).

  --markdown    print the markdown table to stdout instead of opening rofi
  -h, --help    this text

env: KEYBIND_CONF=path   parse that file instead of ~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua

exit: 0 ok · 1 parse failed · 2 bad usage
see: docs/design/shell-and-bars/keybinds.md
```

### `layout-toggle.sh`

invoked by: **SUPER + ALT + L** — layout: dwindle <-> scrolling

```
usage: layout-toggle.sh

Flips the global layout dwindle <-> scrolling (SUPER+ALT+L) through the Lua
API over hyprctl (`repl` reads, `eval` writes). The change lasts until the
next config reload, when hyprland.lua's `general.layout = "dwindle"` wins
again: dwindle is the default, scrolling is a mode you opt into for a session.

  -h, --help    this text

### `lid.sh`

invoked by: **switch:on:Lid Switch** — lid.sh close; **switch:off:Lid Switch** — lid.sh open

```
usage: lid.sh open|close

Enables or disables the internal laptop panel on lid open/close while docked
(the two `switch:*:Lid Switch` binds in hyprland.lua). Monitor changes go
through `hyprctl eval 'hl.monitor{...}'` because this Hyprland build uses the
Lua config (`hyprctl keyword monitor` is rejected). The panel connector is the
first eDP*; re-enable uses the preferred mode and auto position so it comes
back in any dock layout. Does not lock the session (hypridle does).

  close         disable the panel
  open          enable the panel (preferred mode, auto position, scale 1.5)
  -h, --help    this text

exit: 0 ok · 1 hyprctl failed · 2 bad usage
see: dotfiles/.config/hypr/README.md
```

### `monitors-pin.sh`

invoked by: by hand

```
usage: monitors-pin.sh [--print]

Writes ~/.config/dram/monitors.lua: this host's external panels by their description
(`desc:`, which ends in the panel's serial number), left to right as Hyprland places
them: main is the leftmost, mid the next. hyprland.lua and gaming.lua read the file, so
their monitor and workspace rules follow a panel from port to port (a dock renumbers its
DP-* ports). Without the file the rules name cabin's ports, DP-1 and HDMI-A-1. The file
stays on the host: serial numbers are kept out of the repo. Run it once the panels stand
where they belong, then `hyprctl reload`.

  --print     print the file instead of writing it
  -h, --help  this text

exit: 0 written or printed · 1 no Hyprland, or no external panel · 2 bad usage
see: dotfiles/.config/hypr/README.md
```

### `nightlight.sh`

invoked by: **SUPER + ALT + N** — night light toggle

```
usage: nightlight.sh

Blue-light filter toggle (SUPER+ALT+N) via hyprsunset. If a hyprsunset is
already running (hyprland.lua autostarts one; dram-theme-auto drives it by
the sun) the filter is forced to 4000 K over IPC and the next press hands
control back to the sun; if none runs, one is spawned and the next press
kills it. A state file under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR remembers which, so "off"
undoes exactly that and leaves a scheduled instance alive.

  -h, --help    this text

exit: 0 ok · 1 hyprsunset missing · 2 bad usage
see: docs/design/themes/switcher.md
```

```

### `re-lab-tools`

invoked by: by hand

```
usage: re-lab-tools [--dry-run]

The per-user half of the re-lab role (docs/toolchain/profiles/re-lab.md): the uv tools
pinned in packages/uv/re-lab.txt (`uv tool install name==version`, one isolated
environment each) and the Ghidra extensions in packages/ghidra-extensions.tsv built
for the installed Ghidra's major.minor, downloaded, checked against their sha256 and
unpacked into ~/.config/ghidra/ghidra_<version>_PUBLIC/Extensions. Idempotent: a tool
at its pinned version and an extension whose sha256 is recorded are skipped. Re-run
after a Ghidra update (each Ghidra version has its own settings directory). Never root.

### `check-docs.py`

invoked by: `bin/check.sh` §6 (`links see`), §22 (`map`) and §24 (`private`)

```
usage: check-docs.py [--strict] [--list] [map|links|see|private ...] [-- <file> ...]

Checks that the documentation holds together, with the standard library only.

  map      every tracked path matches a rule of docs/map.tsv other than the catch-all;
           every directorate and division of the chart has its page; every page a rule
           names exists
  links    in every tracked *.md at any depth: each relative Markdown link (and its
           #anchor) resolves, and each backticked repo path (`system/...`, `docs/...`)
           exists; docs/history/ (frozen pages) and decisions/0007 (old paths
           tabulated beside the new) are left out
  see      every repo path on a `see:` line of a script or module header exists (and
           its #anchor, when it has one)
  private  tracked text carries none of the words this clone keeps out of the tree:
           addresses, serial numbers, mail addresses and any other term its owner lists
           in <git dir>/info/private.tsv, outside the repo, since a list in the repo
           would publish what it guards; a clone without that file checks nothing
  (none)   all four

  --strict      findings are failures (FAIL lines, exit 1); without it they are warnings
  --list        map: print every tracked path with its directorate, division and branch
  -- <file>...  links, see, private: only these files
  -h, --help    this text

Output lines start with FAIL, WARN or OK; bin/check.sh §6 (links, see), §22 (map) and
§24 (private) run this, in the mode its DOCS_GUARDS switch sets.

exit: 0 no failures · 1 failures (with --strict) · 2 bad usage

```

### `check-pkgnames.py`

invoked by: by hand

```
usage: check-pkgnames.py [--refresh] [--mirror URL]

Checks that every name in packages/*.txt and packages/roles/*.txt (aur.txt
excepted) is something `pacman -S` can resolve: a package, a provided name or a
group in core, extra or multilib — or a [dram] package from pkgs/manifest.txt.
Works without pacman (the Mac): it downloads the three sync databases from an
Arch mirror into ~/.cache/dram/pkgdb/ (re-used for 24 h) and reads them in
memory. A T1-lite: names only, no dependency solving. `bin/check.sh` runs it
when CHECK_PKGDB=1 is set (it needs the network, so it is opt-in).

  --refresh       download the databases even if the cached copies are fresh
  --mirror URL    mirror base (default https://geo.mirror.pkgbuild.com); never
                  archlinux.org, which this LAN cannot reach
  -h, --help      this text

needs:  python3 and network access to an Arch mirror; pkgs/manifest.txt for [dram]
alone:  yes, for any directory of pacman lists: change the paths it reads
here:   bin/check.sh §3 when CHECK_PKGDB=1
exit:   0 every name resolves · 1 unknown names (listed) or a download failed · 2 bad usage

### `check-register.py`

invoked by: by hand

```
usage: check-register.py [--rollout] [--list]

Checks packages/register.tsv, the machine-readable half of decisions/0013: every
name this repo installs must carry a verdict against the three rules (FOSS,
Origin, Community). Names come from four places: the pacman lists
(packages/*.txt + packages/roles/*.txt, aur.txt excepted), the [dram] install set
(pkgs/manifest.txt minus pkgs/BUILD-ONLY), the Flatpak apps (packages/flatpak/<role>.txt, read by
system/flatpak-setup.sh) and the Nix user layer (home.packages lists,
programs.* and ${pkgs.<name>} references in modules/*.nix). Windows has lists
of its own: packages/winget/<role>.txt and host-<host>.txt, one winget:<id>,
msstore:<id> or manual:<name> (a Script unit's or a hand install) per line.

Verdicts: pass · pass-flag (Origin unclear, accepted by a ruling) · waiver
(signed exception; the until column is its re-check date) · swap (decided to go,
the note names the replacement) · pending (awaiting a ruling) · fail (must never
be installed).

Failures: a declared name with no row; an unknown verdict; a duplicate row; a
waiver without a date or past its date; a declared name whose verdict is fail.
Warnings: declared names still marked swap or pending (failures with --rollout,
run before a machine is rebuilt), and rows whose name nothing declares (fail rows
excepted: they exist to forbid).
The Windows names follow the same rules, and besides fail on: a list line that
is not one prefixed name, or a name in two lists; a WinGetPackage unit of a
rendered build (windows/build/<host>/*.winget, decisions/0020) whose package no
list names (an Ensure: Absent one needs a fail row instead); a
Windows row whose note starts "= <name> (Arch)" with another verdict or until
than that Arch row. Windows swap and pending names only warn: --rollout is the
gate of an Arch rebuild.
Output lines start with FAIL, WARN or OK; bin/check.sh §15 runs this.

  --rollout     swap and pending (Arch names) are failures, not warnings
  --list        print every declared name with its source and verdict, then exit 0
  -h, --help    this text

needs:  Python 3 (standard library); the repo's package lists and packages/register.tsv
alone:  yes: start an empty register and point declared() at your own lists
here:   bin/check.sh §15 runs it on every check; CHECK_ROLLOUT=1 adds --rollout
exit:   0 no failures · 1 failures (listed) · 2 bad usage
see:    docs/security/software-supply/register.md, decisions/0013-software-rules-and-waivers.md,
        docs/records/handbook/07-packages.md
```

invoked by: by hand

usage: check-themes.py

The theme-schema invariants, nix-free; run by bin/check.sh §14 (`dram check`).
Reads every dotfiles/.config/themes/<id>/ and prints every rule that fails.

The apps assume every theme dir has the same shape
(dotfiles/.config/themes/README.md → "What each theme file controls"; handbook 6
→ "Adding a theme"), and dram-theme / waybar / the picker read meta.sh by name.

     swaync @accent, swayosd @osd-progress, hyprlock $accent,
     palette.lua accent, kitty cursor_trail_color — except the documented
     EXCEPTIONS below.

Contrast is not measured yet: I have not decided about solarized-paper's

### `check-waybar.py`

invoked by: `bin/check.sh` §10

```
usage: check-waybar.py

The waybar masthead invariants, nix-free; run by bin/check.sh §10 (`dram check`). Reads dotfiles/.config/waybar/ and the waybar-*.sh scripts and prints every rule that fails.

Run by bin/check.sh §10 (`dram check`); exit 1 on any failure.

The rules (dotfiles/.config/waybar/README.md → Captions and spacing). The bar
is words, not icons: a Nerd glyph that slips in brings back the font-metric
gaps this design removed, and a caption outside the house span loses its small
caps and lining figures.

  2. config.jsonc still contains the literal `, "battery"` that
     modules/laptop.nix strips with replaceStrings.

     modules.jsonc, config.jsonc and every waybar-*.sh / waybar-*.py.

     starts with "№ " (U+2116 + space).
  8. style.css defines @define-color rule, resets #workspaces button, gives
     window#waybar its border-bottom, and names no hex colour outside comments.
  9. both bars set "spacing": 0 (style.css owns every gap).

### `forget-host.sh`

invoked by: by hand

```
usage: forget-host.sh <host> [--plan | --execute [--delete-backups] [--dry-run]]

Mac side of retiring a host (the host side is system/decommission.sh).
--plan (the default) prints what --execute would do and changes nothing.
--execute, after the host name typed back: git rm modules/hosts/<host>.nix
and hosts/<host>/ (flake.nix needs no edit: it reads the directory), drops
the host from .sops.yaml (the `# host:` marker, the `&<host>` anchor and
the `*<host>` reference) and runs `sops updatekeys -y secrets/pj.yaml` when
sops is on PATH — it is not on the Mac, so it prints the command to run with
a YubiKey (or on the backup peer, when the host had one) — removes the
host's `<host>=<ip>` entry from the hardcoded list in bin/pull-backups.sh
when it has one, prints the bin/sync-dram-repo.sh lines that name it (which
host is builder and which consumer is a decision, not a sed), then runs
bin/check.sh. The host's address comes from its own file (`address`).
While backups are paused (decisions/0014) there is no peer and no Borg
copy; with one, the Mac's copy of the host's OWN Borg repo,
~/backups/borg/on-<peer>/<host>/, goes only with --delete-backups and a
second typed confirmation, and ~/backups/borg/on-<host>/ (the PEER's repo
as that host stored it) is never deleted here. Peer-side steps and the
UniFi / GitHub steps are printed for you. Nothing is committed. Runs on the
Mac (bash 3.2).

  --plan              print the plan (default)
  --execute           do it, after the typed host name
  --delete-backups    with --execute: also rm -rf ~/backups/borg/on-<peer>/<host>
  --dry-run           with --execute: print the commands, change nothing, no prompt
  -h, --help          this text

needs:  git, awk, sed; sops for the recipient update (it prints the command without);
        install/lib/roles.sh, .sops.yaml, bin/pull-backups.sh, bin/check.sh
alone:  no: it edits this repo's host files, .sops.yaml and the pull list
here:   by hand on the Mac, after system/decommission.sh --plan on the host
exit:   0 ok · 1 refused (unknown host, name mismatch, no terminal) or check.sh failed · 2 bad usage
see:    docs/records/handbook/10-teardown.md, docs/operations/releases/README.md
```

### `gen-browser-css.py`

invoked by: by hand on the Mac (dev-time); commit the output

```
usage: gen-browser-css.py [theme ...]

Writes the browser/mail chrome palette (themes/<t>/browser.css) for every dram theme, or for the named ones. A dev-time generator: run it after editing a theme's palette and commit the output; dram-theme only links the files.

LibreWolf and Thunderbird take their chrome from a userChrome.css in the PROFILE
dir. The rules are static and tracked once (dotfiles/.librewolf/chrome/userChrome.css,
dotfiles/.thunderbird-chrome/userChrome.css); the colours are this file's output,
one per theme, which both sheets @import as `letterpress-colors.css`:

    dotfiles/.config/themes/<t>/waybar.css   base/mantle/crust/text/subtext/overlay/
                                             surface0/surface1/red/green/yellow/blue
  + dotfiles/.config/themes/<t>/palette.lua  accent, accent_dim (the ONE accent ink)
  + dotfiles/.config/themes/<t>/meta.sh      COLOR_SCHEME (prefer-light -> light derivations)
  = dotfiles/.config/themes/<t>/browser.css  `:root { color-scheme: dark; --lp-base: … }`

dram-theme links <profile>/chrome/letterpress-colors.css -> themes/current/browser.css,
so a theme switch swaps the colours without touching the rules. The file defines
ONLY --lp-* custom properties (+ color-scheme): the mapping onto Firefox's and
Thunderbird's own variables lives in the two userChrome.css files, where it is
reviewed against the app's stylesheet version (dotfiles/.librewolf/README.md).
Same light/dark derivations as bin/gen-gtk-css.py:

    view   = mantle (dark) | base mixed 45 % toward white (light)   the reading surface
    raised = surface0 (dark) | view (light)                          popovers, menus, panels
    rule   = alpha(text, .18)   the hairline       shade = alpha(text, .10)
    hover  = alpha(text, .08)   active = alpha(text, .14)   faint = alpha(text, .55)
    accent_fg = best contrast of white / crust / text on the accent

Run from anywhere:  python3 bin/gen-browser-css.py [theme ...]
No arguments = every theme dir. Idempotent; prints the files it rewrote.

  theme ...     theme dir ids under dotfiles/.config/themes (default: every theme)

invoked by: `bin/check.sh` §23 (`--check`); by hand after a module README's fact box changes

```
usage: gen-catalogue.py [--check]

Writes docs/catalogue.md, the list of every part of this repo that can be copied on
its own, from the fact box at the top of each module's README:

    | | |
    |---|---|
    | Needs | <software and the version tested, with the month; files from elsewhere> |
    | Copy alone | <yes / yes, after one change / no, and why> |
    | License | <MIT, or the licenses of the files that differ> |

Three rows, these labels, in this order (Licence is read as License). The README's
title names the module, its directory is where it lives, and docs/map.tsv places it
under a directorate and a division. Every tracked README.md and REVIEW.md outside docs/
and decisions/ is read; a table that starts like the box and names Copy alone or
License but breaks the shape is an error. Deterministic: running it twice produces no
diff. Needs only python3 and git; runs on the Mac. bin/check.sh §23 runs it with --check.

  --check       write nothing; exit 1 (with a diff) when docs/catalogue.md is stale
  -h, --help    this text

exit: 0 ok · 1 --check found a difference, or a fact box is malformed · 2 bad usage
see: docs/records/templates/module.md, docs/map.tsv
```

### `gen-gtk-css.py`

invoked by: by hand on the Mac (dev-time); commit the output

```
usage: gen-gtk-css.py [theme ...]

Recolours adw-gtk3 / libadwaita for every dram theme, or for the named ones: writes themes/<t>/gtk.css (GTK4) and gtk3.css (GTK3) from the theme's palette. A dev-time generator; commit the output.

One GTK theme (adw-gtk3, pacman `adw-gtk-theme`) serves all 17 dram themes; the
colours come from two generated user stylesheets per theme, written here:

    dotfiles/.config/themes/<t>/waybar.css   base/mantle/crust/text/surface0/red/green/yellow
                                             (+accent fallback)
  + dotfiles/.config/themes/<t>/palette.lua  accent (the one accent ink)
  + dotfiles/.config/themes/<t>/meta.sh      COLOR_SCHEME (prefer-light -> light derivations)
  = dotfiles/.config/themes/<t>/gtk.css      GTK4 / libadwaita: `:root { --accent-bg-color }`
                                             variables, the legacy `@define-color` aliases,
                                             and the Letterpress chrome (3 px radii, hairlines,
                                             no heavy shadows)
  = dotfiles/.config/themes/<t>/gtk3.css     GTK3 / adw-gtk3: `@define-color` ONLY

dram-theme links ~/.config/gtk-4.0/gtk.css -> themes/current/gtk.css and
~/.config/gtk-3.0/gtk.css -> themes/current/gtk3.css. Two files because GTK3
cannot parse `:root { --var }` (it would log a parse error in every GTK3 app),
and gtk3.css carries no selector rules: GTK loads the user stylesheet
at GTK_STYLE_PROVIDER_PRIORITY_USER (800), above an application's own CSS (600),
so a `button {}` rule there would restyle waybar and nwg-drawer, both GTK3, over
their themed stylesheets. Named colours are harmless (the
libadwaita names do not collide with the waybar.css palette names).

Colour mapping (palette field -> GTK named colour / variable):
    base      -> window_bg, headerbar_bg (flat page: the headerbar is the window)
    mantle    -> view_bg (dark) | sidebar_bg
    base+white-> view_bg (light: a lighter step derived from base)
    surface0  -> card_bg, popover_bg, dialog_bg, thumbnail_bg (dark); light uses view_bg
    text      -> every *_fg colour, and the hairline alpha(text, .18)
    accent    -> accent_bg_color, accent_color; accent_fg = best contrast of white/crust/text
    red       -> destructive_*, error_*     green -> success_*     yellow -> warning_*

Run from anywhere:  python3 bin/gen-gtk-css.py [theme ...]
No arguments = every theme dir. Idempotent; prints the files it rewrote.
See docs/design/themes/generators.md ("GTK").

  theme ...     theme dir ids under dotfiles/.config/themes (default: every theme)
  -h, --help    this text

exit: 0 ok · 1 a theme failed to render · 2 bad usage
see: docs/design/themes/generators.md
```

### `gen-tui-themes.py`

invoked by: by hand on the Mac (dev-time); commit the output

```
usage: gen-tui-themes.py [theme ...]

Writes every theme's btop.theme and cava.theme (or the named themes') in the Letterpress style from the theme's palette. A dev-time generator; commit the output.

The two TUI monitors are the printed page again: paper (the terminal's own
background, so kitty's grain shows through), ink text, hairline boxes, and ONE
accent ink that carries every graph as a three-stop gradient from a faint tint of
itself to the full colour. Nothing is a rainbow.

    dotfiles/.config/themes/<t>/waybar.css   base/text/subtext/overlay/surface0/surface1/red
  + dotfiles/.config/themes/<t>/palette.lua  accent (the ONE accent ink)
  = dotfiles/.config/themes/<t>/btop.theme   (committed — dram-theme points color_theme at it)
  = dotfiles/.config/themes/<t>/cava.theme   (committed — dram-theme splices its [color] block)

Mapping (palette field -> btop key / cava key):
    (empty)              -> main_bg                 terminal background; btop.conf also sets
                                                    theme_background = false
    text                 -> main_fg, title          ink; box captions are bold ink
    accent               -> hi_fg, selected_fg      the rubric: hotkey letters, the cursor row
    surface0             -> selected_bg
    overlay              -> inactive_fg
    subtext              -> graph_text, proc_misc
    surface1             -> meter_bg
    mix(base,subtext,.4) -> cpu_box mem_box net_box proc_box div_line   one hairline grey
    faint -> mid -> accent  cpu_*, free_*, used_*, available_*, download_*, process_*
                            (faint = accent mixed 55 % toward the paper, mid = 25 %)
    faint -> mid -> subtext cached_*, upload_*      the muted second tone
    faint -> accent -> red  temp_*                  warm within the accent hue; red only at the end
    cava: gradient_count = 3 (faint, mid, accent), foreground = text, background = default

Run from anywhere:  python3 bin/gen-tui-themes.py [theme ...]
No arguments = every theme dir. Idempotent; prints the files it rewrote.

### `gen-vscode-themes.py`

invoked by: by hand on the Mac (dev-time); commit the output

```
usage: gen-vscode-themes.py [theme ...]

Writes one VS Code colour theme per dram theme (or per named theme) into the local extension dotfiles/.vscode/extensions/letterpress-themes, and its package.json on a full run. A dev-time generator; commit the output; codium-themes-install registers the extension.

The editor is the printed page again: every workbench surface is the paper
(`base`), panels and widgets are the mantle, the chrome is separated by 1 px
hairlines in alpha(text, .18) instead of coloured bars, and ONE accent ink
carries the cursor, the focus ring, links, the active tab's rule, the find
match and the badges. Syntax is set in five inks: body ink, the accent for
keywords, a second (ochre) tone for strings, blue/teal for types, subtext
italic for comments. No bold, no rainbow brackets.

    dotfiles/.config/themes/<t>/waybar.css   base mantle crust text subtext overlay
                                             surface0 surface1 red green yellow blue
                                             teal peach mauve
  + dotfiles/.config/themes/<t>/palette.lua  accent, accent_dim (the ONE accent ink)
  + dotfiles/.config/themes/<t>/meta.sh      COLOR_SCHEME (light/dark), MENU_NAME (label)
  + dotfiles/.config/themes/<t>/kitty.conf   color0..15 -> the integrated terminal
  = dotfiles/.vscode/extensions/letterpress-themes/themes/letterpress-<t>-color-theme.json
  = dotfiles/.vscode/extensions/letterpress-themes/package.json   (contributes.themes)

Workbench mapping (palette field -> VS Code colour key):
    base              -> editor, sideBar, activityBar, statusBar, titleBar, tabs,
                         panel, terminal, breadcrumbs: every surface is the paper
    mantle            -> input, dropdown, editorWidget (find/suggest/hover),
                         quickInput, notifications, menu, peekView, sticky scroll hover
    alpha(text,.18)   -> every *.border key (hairlines); .12 for indent guides
    accent            -> focusBorder, editorCursor, textLink, button, badge,
                         activityBarBadge, tab.activeBorderTop, activityBar.activeBorder,
                         panelTitle.activeBorder, progressBar, peekView.border,
                         list.highlightForeground, inputOption.activeBorder
    alpha(accent,…)   -> list.activeSelectionBackground (.20), editor.findMatch (.40 / .35),
                         findMatchHighlight (.18), selectionHighlight (.12), bracket match
    alpha(text,.14)   -> editor.selectionBackground (a neutral grey, never an accent fill)
    subtext           -> editorLineNumber, descriptions, inactive tabs/titles, icons
    overlay           -> disabled text, placeholders, code lens, inactive activity icons
    red/yellow/blue   -> editorError / editorWarning / editorInfo, gutter + diff colours,
    green                git decorations (modified = yellow, added = green, deleted = red)
    kitty color0..15  -> terminal.ansi*
Token colours (TextMate scope -> ink):
    comment                     subtext italic
    string, markup.inline.raw   yellow  (the second tone; raised to >= 4.5:1 on the paper)
    keyword, storage            accent
    entity.name.type/class      blue;  support.type, namespace, HTML tag -> teal
    constant.numeric/language   numbers = accent_dim on light, accent mixed toward
                                the ink on dark (accent_dim is too dark on a dark page)
    function, variable, operator  text (plain weight)
    punctuation                 subtext
    invalid                     red

Run from anywhere:  python3 bin/gen-vscode-themes.py [theme ...]
No arguments = every theme dir (package.json is written only on a full run).
Idempotent; prints the files it rewrote. VERSION is bumped by hand — a run date
would rewrite package.json daily.
See dotfiles/.vscode/extensions/letterpress-themes/README.md.

  theme ...     theme dir ids under dotfiles/.config/themes (default: every theme)
  -h, --help    this text

exit: 0 ok · 1 a theme failed to render · 2 bad usage
see: dotfiles/.vscode/extensions/letterpress-themes/README.md
```

invoked by: by hand on the Mac after a palette change (commit the output); `bin/check.sh` §19 (`--check`)

usage: gen-windows-look.py [theme] [--check]

Writes install/windows/letterpress/, the Letterpress look for Windows and its apps, from the palette files Arch already uses. A dev-time generator like gen-browser-css.py: run it after editing a palette and commit the output; install/windows/apply-windows.sh copies the directory to C:\ProgramData\dram\letterpress, where the desktop role's units (windows/roles/desktop.nix) and dram-windows/look.ps1 put it in place (docs/design/themes/windows.md).

    dotfiles/.config/themes/<t>/kitty.conf   color0-15, foreground, background, cursor, selection
  + dotfiles/.config/themes/<t>/waybar.css   base mantle crust text subtext overlay surface0/1, hues
  + dotfiles/.config/themes/<t>/palette.lua  accent, accent_dim (the ONE accent ink)
  + dotfiles/.config/themes/<t>/meta.sh      COLOR_SCHEME (light/dark), MENU_NAME
  + bin/gen-vscode-themes.py                 the syntax inks (readable(): >= 4.5:1 on the paper)
                                             and the pj.letterpress-themes extension it writes
  + install/windows/upstream/                Notepad++ v8.9.8.1 DarkModeDefault.xml (GPL-2.0),
                                             Mumble v1.5.939 Dark.qss (Unlicense; its header names the WTFPL) and Wireshark
                                             v4.6.9 colorfilters (GPL-2.0-or-later), recoloured by name
  + dotfiles/.config/waybar/{config,modules}.jsonc  the masthead's layout, captions, intervals
  = install/windows/letterpress/
      theme                  the theme id the directory was generated from
      wt-schemes.json        Windows Terminal fragment: every dram theme as a colour scheme
      wt-settings.json       the keys look.ps1 owns in Windows Terminal's settings.json
      wsl/terminal-profile.json  profile template for the WSL Arch clone (scheme + font)
      psreadline.ps1         PSReadLine and $PSStyle in the inks; dot-sourced by the profile
      conhost.json           HKCU\Console ColorTable00-15 (the unit conhost-letterpress)
      accent.json            accent DWORDs + AccentPalette (the unit letterpress-look)
      vscodium-settings.json the keys look.ps1 pins in VSCodium's settings.json
      pj.letterpress-themes-<version>.vsix   the extension, packed for `codium --install-extension`
      powertoys.json         per utility, the colour keys of its PowerToys settings.json
      cmdpal.json            Command Palette's colour keys (washi paper behind the list)
      windirstat.json        WinDirStat's registry colours (tree bars, treemap highlight)
      runelite.json          RuneLite's overlay colour, for every profile
      vesktop/ obs/ notepad++/ mumble/ halloy/ qbittorrent/ calibre/ vortex/ mintty/
      teamspeak/ nomacs/ wireshark/
                             one theme (and the keys that select it) per app
      zebar/                 the masthead: Waybar's bar as a Zebar widget pack (letterpress/:
                             zpack.json, masthead.html/.css/.js) and settings.json starting it;
                             look.ps1 puts both in %USERPROFILE%\.glzr\zebar

Deterministic (no dates, fixed zip timestamps, a fixed @version: VERSION below, bumped by hand),
so --check can compare; bin/check.sh section 19 runs it. Every text output is ASCII, and every
ink the TeamSpeak, nomacs and Wireshark outputs set on a paper reads at 4.5:1 or better (the
build fails otherwise). Without a theme argument it regenerates the theme the directory was
made from (washi, the house theme, when there is none).

  theme         a theme dir id under dotfiles/.config/themes (default: the recorded one, else washi)
  --check       write nothing; exit 1 with a diff when the directory is stale
  -h, --help    this text

exit: 0 ok (or up to date) · 1 stale (--check) or an input failed · 2 bad usage
see: docs/design/themes/windows.md

### `gen-yazi-flavors.py`

invoked by: by hand on the Mac (dev-time); commit the output

```
usage: gen-yazi-flavors.py [theme ...]

Writes a Letterpress yazi flavor per dram theme (or per named theme) under dotfiles/.config/yazi/flavors/. A dev-time generator; commit the output.

yazi is the printed page again: paper is the terminal's own background (no
`bg` anywhere yazi lets us leave it out, so kitty's grain shows through), ink
text, hairline rules, and ONE accent ink. The cursor row is accent ink on the
`surface0` tint, not a reversed-video block; the mode word in the status bar is
a plain bold word in the accent, not a powerline pill; the file-type colours
are restrained (dirs in the accent's dim ink, executables green, symlinks
italic, media and archives in the muted inks). No Nerd-font icons: the
`[icon]` tables are emptied and the few glyphs yazi prints by itself (notify,
completion) are typographic marks, never private-use codepoints.

        tmtheme.xml   a minimal TextMate theme for the code preview

    accent_dim (lifted to      filetype `*/` (directories, bold), marker_marked

    surface0                   indicator.* bg (the cursor row), count_* bg, hovered rows
    surface1                   input.selected bg, progress bg
    text                       which.desc, help.action, progress_label
    subtext                    symlink_target, find_position, tabs.inactive, mode.*_alt,

                               images (plain) and audio/video (italic)
    overlay                    which.rest, perm_sep, archives, vfs ghosts
    mix(base, subtext, .40)    every border (one hairline grey, like btop's boxes)
    yellow                     marker_copied, count_copied, mode.select_main, strings
    red                        marker_cut, count_cut, mode.unset_main, orphans, errors
    green                      executables, perm_exec, notify info, diff inserted
    blue / teal / peach / mauve  tmtheme only: types, attributes, numbers, tags

### `pkgs.sh`

invoked by: `dram pkgs <cmd>`; `bin/check.sh` §12 (`check`)

```
usage: pkgs.sh <check|update|build|publish|log|list|key> [args]

Operates the [dram] package repo from ~/git/dotfiles on a host; `dram pkgs
<cmd>` dispatches here. Every PKGBUILD under pkgs/ is reviewed, pinned and
signed; `check` runs on the Mac too (pacman checks skipped).

  check   [name...]     every pkgs/<name> is in the manifest at its .SRCINFO
                        version, no official-repo name is shadowed (unless in
                        pkgs/OVERRIDES), every source is pinned (no -git, no
                        pkgver(), no SKIP outside a git checkout, no md5),
                        .SRCINFO / UPSTREAM / REVIEW.md present, signing keys vendored
  update  [name...]     clone the AUR repo, show `git diff <UPSTREAM>..HEAD`
                        (PKGBUILD, *.install, hooks) in $PAGER; on `y` apply
                        the AUR delta on top of our copy, show the PIN note,
                        $EDITOR, updpkgsums, makepkg --printsrcinfo, rewrite
                        UPSTREAM + manifest.txt, git commit
  build   [name...]     makechrootpkg -c -u in /var/lib/archbuild/dram-x86_64,
                        local build deps fed in with -I from /srv/dram, every
                        package file detached-signed with the key in
                        ~/.config/dram/gpgkey, line appended to pkgs/BUILDLOG
  publish               repo-add -s -R into /srv/dram/dram.db, rsync to
                        /var/lib/dram-repo on THIS host. The other host gets
                        the repo from the Mac (bin/sync-dram-repo.sh): the
                        hosts' ssh keys for each other are pinned to `borg
                        serve`, so there is no host-to-host path (the old
                        `--no-peer` flag is accepted and ignored; `sync` is gone)
  log     <pkgfile...>  append "name version sha256 date" to pkgs/BUILDLOG
  list    [--install|--repo]
                        manifest names. --repo: minus pkgs/BUILD-ONLY (what a host
                        can install from [dram]). --install: the every-host set,
                        --repo minus the names a packages list claims (a [dram]
                        name in packages/roles/gaming.txt installs with that role
                        through dram apply, not on every host)
  key     [--new|--uid] the signing key: its fingerprint, expiry and whether
                        pkgs/dram.asc and system/pacman-dram-repo.sh agree with it.
                        --new (the builder, as the user, once per key): gpg makes an
                        ed25519 signing key (asks a passphrase), writes
                        ~/.config/dram/gpgkey, exports pkgs/dram.asc and pins its
                        fingerprint in system/pacman-dram-repo.sh — one commit.
                        --uid (the builder, as the user): gives the key this
                        script's user ID, revokes its others and exports
                        pkgs/dram.asc with that one (the same key: hosts keep it)
  -h, --help            this text

env: DRAM_GPGKEY    signing key fingerprint (else ~/.config/dram/gpgkey)
     PACKAGER       makepkg PACKAGER; also PAGER, EDITOR

exit: 0 ok · 1 a check or step failed · 2 bad usage
see: docs/toolchain/packaging/README.md
```

```
usage: pull-backups.sh [--check]

The Mac's side of the backups: pulls each host's Borg repository (which lives
on the other host, backups/borg/<peer>) into ~/backups/borg/on-<host>/, so
the Mac holds a copy of both. Per host, over one multiplexed ssh connection
(ControlMaster: the 2026-10-06 06:05 pull died in rsync's second handshake
right after a successful probe): a probe; then a staging step on the host,
where `borg with-lock` copies each repo under ~/backups/borg/ to
~/backups/borg-stage/<name>/ while holding the Borg lock (no passphrase
needed; lock.exclusive/lock.roster are left out), so the copy is never
mid-transaction; then an rsync --delete of backups/borg-stage/ into
on-<host>/ (one retry after 30 s). Layout on the Mac is unchanged:
on-<host>/<peer-repo>/. A host that is off is skipped; a host whose
on-<host>/.pulled marker is younger than 20 h is skipped too (the launchd
job also runs at every login, RunAtLoad). At the end, a WARN line per host
whose copy is older than 2 days or has no marker yet. Scheduled by
install/mac-launchd.sh (daily 06:00 and at login, after the 03:00 host
backups); run by hand any time. Log: ~/backups/borg/pull.log. Runs on the
Mac (bash 3.2, openrsync); the hosts need borg + rsync (packages/base.txt).

  --check       read-only: print the age of each host's copy; exit 1 when one
                is older than 2 days or was never pulled. Touches nothing.
  -h, --help    this text

needs:  ssh, rsync or openrsync; borg and rsync on the hosts; install/lib/roles.sh and
        each host file's address and backupPeer
alone:  yes, after replacing the host lookup with a list of your own hosts
here:   paused with the backups until the NAS (decisions/0014): it pulls only hosts whose
        file names a backupPeer; install/mac-launchd.sh schedules it
exit:   0 ok · 1 a staging or rsync step failed, or (--check) a copy is stale or missing · 2 bad usage
see:    docs/operations/backups/README.md
```

### `push-host.sh`

invoked by: by hand on the Mac; `bin/release.sh` for every host with `dram.address`

```
usage: push-host.sh <ssh-target> [branch] [--force] | --wsl <host> <windows-ssh-target> [branch]

Pushes this repo's committed state to a host's ~/git/dotfiles without
touching gitignored runtime state there (themes/current, cava/config, the
files dram-theme writes): git bundle (the branch + every tag) -> ssh pipe ->
`git fetch` on the host. The hosts have no remote, so this is how release
tags (bin/release.sh) and master reach them. What happens to the checkout
depends on the host's channel (dram channel, docs/operations/releases/README.md):
  on a branch (channel main)        `git reset --hard` to the pushed tip, as before
  detached at a release (stable)    refs updated, checkout untouched; `dram update`
                                    there moves it to the newest tag
Tracked files update in place; untracked and ignored files are left alone.
On a branch the host side refuses to reset over uncommitted edits to tracked
files and names them: commit or stash them there, or pass --force to discard.
A detached (stable) host is never reset, so its edits are left as they are.
Needs a clean working tree here. Runs on the Mac.

--wsl <host>: a WSL clone (form = "wsl" in modules/hosts/<host>.nix, decisions/0021)
has no ssh of its own. The bundle goes to its Windows PC's OpenSSH instead
(HostKeyAlias <wsl.windowsHost>-win, as install/windows/apply-windows.sh connects) and
is staged as C:\ProgramData\dram\dotfiles.bundle, beside what
dram-windows/wsl.ps1 builds the clone with (wsl.ps1, wslconfig, wsl.conf). In the
clone `dram update` receives it first (dram receive). Nothing runs in the clone from
here; a failed connection (Windows off, or cabin booted into Arch) changes nothing.

  branch        the branch to push (default: the current one)
  --force       discard uncommitted edits to tracked files on the host
  -h, --help    this text

needs:  git, ssh, scp; install/lib/roles.sh for --wsl; ~/git/dotfiles cloned on the host
alone:  yes, for hosts without a git remote: change the ~/git/dotfiles path in the
        host-side block
here:   bin/release.sh runs it for each host with dram.address; by hand on the Mac
env:    DRAM_WIN_SSH   extra ssh/scp options for --wsl (as for apply-windows.sh)
exit:   0 ok · 1 dirty tree here, uncommitted edits there, or ssh failed · 2 bad usage
see:    docs/operations/releases/pushes.md, docs/platforms/wsl/README.md
```

### `push-windows.sh`

invoked by: by hand on the Mac, for a Windows PC (`docs/operations/releases/pushes.md`); `tests/push-windows.sh` (`bin/check.sh` §19)

```
usage: push-windows.sh <host> [--apply] [--dry-run] [--to USER@ADDR] [--force]

Puts a Windows host's release on it (decisions/0020, docs/operations/releases/pushes.md): the flake's render
of the host (windows/build/<host>/: manifest.json and the winget documents, its release and
commit filled in) and every file its manifest lists, staged from this commit the way
install/windows/apply-windows.sh stages them (install/lib/windows-stage.sh: each from the
source the manifest names - the repo, the render, the fonts and cursors of fonts.pin and
cursors.pin, each download refused unless its sha256 is pinned). Every file's sha256 must be
what the manifest says, so a stale render or a changed source stops here, before anything is
copied; bin/render-windows.sh --check runs first when the renderer is in the tree. Then
dram.ps1 on Windows takes it: `dram receive` checks every file again and switches
C:\ProgramData\dram to the release; --apply also converges.

Only what changed travels: the host's build\files.sha256 (its live release) is read first,
and a file already there with the same sha256 is not sent; the render, the engine (dram.ps1)
and the full list always are. They land in C:\ProgramData\dram\incoming, and the incoming
dram.ps1 runs the receive, so the first push installs dram (dram.cmd on the machine PATH)
and a release can change dram itself. Also staged: build\push.json (this commit's version,
build and commit) and build\packages.tsv (the winget and Store ids the documents declare,
for dram harvest and rollback). Windows' OpenSSH runs cmd.exe: every remote command here is
one plain cmd line, or one `powershell -File` with nothing after it.

Address: --to, else address (and user) in windows/hosts/<host>.nix, else that of the WSL
clone whose wsl.windowsHost is <host> without -win (the clone's address is its PC's). The
host key is checked as HostKeyAlias <host> on a connection of its own (never multiplexed),
so Arch answering at the same address is refused, not written to. Needs a clean tree.

  --apply          then dram apply: each phase's documents and scripts, the desktop step
  --dry-run        nothing on Windows changes but dram's staging area: without --apply the
                   release is checked in incoming\ (dram receive -DryRun), not switched; with
                   it, received, then dram apply -DryRun (winget configure test, -DryRun)
  --to USER@ADDR   the ssh target, instead of the host files'
  --force          dram receive -Force: a push the host's channel (stable: tagged releases
                   only) or its computer name would refuse
  -h, --help       this text

needs:  git, ssh, scp, python3, curl, bsdtar; install/lib/windows-stage.sh and the
        committed render in windows/build/<host>/; Windows' OpenSSH on the PC
alone:  no: it stages from this repo's render and pins, for dram.ps1 on the PC
here:   by hand on the Mac after bin/render-windows.sh; tests/push-windows.sh runs it
        against stand-ins (bin/check.sh §19)
env:    DRAM_WIN_SSH   extra ssh/scp options, before this script's own (for example -i KEY)
exit:   0 received (and applied) · 1 a check, the copy, the receive or the apply failed ·
        2 bad usage
see:    docs/operations/releases/pushes.md, docs/operations/dram/windows.md,
        install/windows/dram-windows/dram.ps1
```

### `release.sh`

invoked by: by hand on the Mac, when a batch is ready for the hosts (`docs/operations/releases/README.md`)

```
usage: release.sh -m "<summary>" [--dry-run] [--checkpoint] [--no-push]

Cuts a release on the Mac. A build is a commit; a release is an annotated
tag vYYYY.MM.N on one (calendar, like SteamOS build ids). In order:
  1. the tree is clean, on master, and `bash bin/check.sh` is green
  2. the next tag for today: vYYYY.MM.N, N = 1 + the highest N this month
  3. CHANGELOG.md gets a section at the top: the tag and the date, the summary,
     then the commits since the previous tag grouped Removed, Added, Changed,
     Fixed, Security by each commit's `Changelog:` trailer (no trailer: Changed;
     `Changelog: skip` leaves the commit out; docs/records/changelog.md)
  4. commit "release vX: <summary>", then `git tag -a vX -m "<summary>"`
  5. bin/push-host.sh <user>@<address> for every modules/hosts/*.nix that sets
     dram.address (tags ride in the bundle). A host on channel stable moves
     to the tag with `dram update` there; one on main is reset to it now.
     A WSL clone (form = "wsl") gets `push-host.sh --wsl`: the bundle is staged
     on its Windows PC, and a failure there (Windows off, or cabin in Arch) is
     a warning, not a failed release: the clone catches up at the next push.

  -m <summary>   one line for the tag annotation and the CHANGELOG section (required unless --dry-run)
  --checkpoint   a build every host must pass through: the word "checkpoint"
                 goes into the annotation and `dram update` stops at it
  --dry-run      print the tag, the CHANGELOG section and the push targets; change nothing
  --no-push      commit and tag, skip the pushes (bin/push-host.sh later)
  -h, --help     this text

needs:  git, ssh; bin/check.sh, bin/push-host.sh, install/lib/roles.sh; runs on the Mac
alone:  yes, with a push script and a check script of your own; releases are cut
        from master and the hosts' addresses come from modules/hosts/*.nix
here:   by hand on the Mac; CHANGELOG.md is its output, and dram changelog reads it
exit:   0 ok · 1 dirty tree, not on master, check.sh failed, nothing new, or a push failed · 2 bad usage
see:    docs/operations/releases/README.md
```

### `render-windows.sh`

invoked by: by hand on the Mac (or Arch) after a change under `windows/`, `packages/winget/` or the rice (commit `windows/build/`); `bin/check.sh` §19 (`--check`); `install/windows/apply-windows.sh` (`--check`)

```
usage: render-windows.sh [HOST...] [--check] [--lock]

Renders each Windows host of windows/hosts/ (default: every one) from the flake into
windows/build/<HOST>/ (decisions/0020, docs/platforms/windows/renderer.md): its winget
configuration documents, one per phase and scope, manifest.json (what the converge runs, in
order, and every file it stages with its sha256) and inputs.json (every repo file the render
read). Commit the result: install/windows/apply-windows.sh applies a committed build and
refuses a stale one. Nix evaluates where it is installed (Arch); on the Mac in a throwaway
nixos/nix container under Colima (decisions/log.md#d26; DOCKER_CONTEXT, default colima), fed
the tracked files on stdin - what a host's flake sees - with its downloads cached in the
docker volume dram-nix-cache. When
install/windows/fonts.pin has moved past install/windows/fonts.lock, the lock is written again
first (the pinned downloads, cached in ~/.cache/dram/fonts; bsdtar), since Nix downloads
nothing and the manifest lists every font file.

  --check     no Nix, no network: every committed build is current (each file of its
              inputs.json hashed again, the directories it read listed again from git, the
              Markdown pages under windows/ aside) and every host file has a build;
              bin/check.sh §19 runs it
  --lock      write install/windows/fonts.lock again even if fonts.pin has not moved
  -h, --help  this text

exit: 0 rendered, or current · 1 a stale build, a failed lock or a failed render · 2 bad usage
see: windows/default.nix, docs/platforms/windows/renderer.md
```

### `repro.sh`

invoked by: by hand

```
usage: repro.sh [-n|--dry-run] [pkg ...] | --ours <name|file.pkg.tar.zst>

Reproducibility spot-check; runs on an Arch host. Without --ours it rebuilds
official packages in a clean container (archlinux-repro: `repro <file>`) and
reports reproducible / NOT reproducible per package; the default set is
linux linux-lts hyprland openssh sudo systemd pacman (the kernel, the
compositor, the remote door, the privilege boundary, init, the package
manager). --ours <name> builds the vendored pkgs/<name> twice with the same
SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH and diffoscopes the outputs; --ours <file.pkg.tar.zst>
rebuilds the package that file came from once (its .BUILDINFO builddate
becomes SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH) and diffoscopes the rebuild against the file — or,
when every package in the file's build chroot was official, hands it to
`repro -f` run from pkgs/<name> (-f = use the local PKGBUILD) for an
independent rebuild from the Arch archive. Logs: ~/.local/state/dram/repro/.

  pkg ...            official packages to check (default: the set above)
  --ours TARGET      a vendored package name, or a .pkg.tar.zst file
  -n, --dry-run      print the commands, run nothing
  -h, --help         this text

needs:  an Arch host, archlinux-repro, sudo (systemd-nspawn); diffoscope and devtools for --ours
alone:  yes on Arch for official packages; --ours wants a pkgs/<name>/ recipe layout
here:   by hand, monthly and after an update to the kernel, Hyprland, openssh, sudo,
        systemd or pacman; logs in ~/.local/state/dram/repro/
exit:   0 all reproducible · 1 one was not, or a build failed (repro exits 1 for both) · 2 bad usage
see:    docs/security/software-supply/integrity.md
```

### `serve-repo.sh`

invoked by: by hand

```
usage: serve-repo.sh [--port N | --out FILE]

Hands this repo to a machine booted from the Arch ISO (handbook 01 §4): a clone of the
checked-out branch with every release tag (the installed host's `dram update` follows
the tags), packed as a tar — the ISO has curl and tar but no git — with its sha256 and
the commands to type in the ISO, served over HTTP on this machine's LAN address until
Ctrl-C. Only committed work travels (a clean tree is required, and the clone is made
from a bundle of the branch); the sha256 typed in the ISO is what proves the download
is the tar made here. No macOS ._* metadata files. Runs on the Mac (or any machine
with git, tar and python3).

### `yubikey.sh`

invoked by: by hand

```
usage: yubikey.sh <status | enroll <label> [--no-age] | ssh [<label>] | use <label>>

The YubiKeys (decisions/0019); `dram yubikey` runs this. The public
halves live in keys/ssh.pub, keys/pam-u2f.txt and .sops.yaml, committed on the Mac;
nothing here writes the repo. Runs as the login user on an Arch host, never root.

                       factor (the full check is `dram doctor`)

                       resident SSH key (application ssh:dram-<label>), the pam-u2f
                       credential (origin pam://dram) and, unless --no-age, an age

                       ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_sk to <label>'s (default: the first in
                       keys/ssh.pub whose handle is here)

                       and git's signing key, modules/dev.nix) at another key's handle

The system layer (`/etc`, the ESP, the initramfs): `sudo bash system/<script>`; every writer has `--dry-run`.

Writes the ly greeter config from the house palette
(system/house-palette.sh): /etc/ly/config.ini, or config.lua where ly reads
that (autodetected). Write-on-change; the previous file is kept once as
config.<ext>.bak-<stamp>. The ly `dur` animation is refused and scrubbed

  --anim none|matrix   animation; default none (`none` / `matrix` also accepted bare)
  --dry-run            no root needed; shows what would change

### `apply-refind.sh`

invoked by: `system-dram.sh` (a `dram apply` hook); by hand

```
usage: apply-refind.sh [--theme letterpress|catppuccin] [--dry-run]

rEFInd as the themed boot menu in front of the UKI chain (docs/platforms/arch/boot-chain.md;
decisions/0011, 2026-10-12): firmware -> rEFInd -> a signed UKI, Windows or systemd-boot
-> Plymouth -> ly. Copies /usr/share/refind/refind_x64.efi to <ESP>/EFI/refind/, signed
by sbctl when it has keys (tracked, so it is signed again on every refind upgrade by
/usr/local/lib/dram/refind-update through /etc/pacman.d/hooks/99-refind.hook, both
installed here); system/refind-<theme>/ as the theme; a refind.conf with one entry per
boot target on the ESP: Arch Linux, Arch Linux LTS, Windows, and "Snapshots & recovery"
(systemd-boot, whose menu keeps the fallback and snapshot UKIs). Windows on its own ESP
(label WIN-ESP) is started through its firmware entry (firmware_bootnum), never loaded by
rEFInd; without one, the tile loads /EFI/Microsoft/Boot/bootmgfw.efi from this ESP. Puts the NVRAM entry
"rEFInd" first in BootOrder; systemd-boot's entry stays behind it, so the firmware
falls back to systemd-boot if rEFInd ever fails. The MSI firmware reshuffles BootOrder
when drives come or go: dram-refind-first.service (installed and enabled here) puts
rEFInd first again at every boot, moving nothing else. Write-on-change with one .bak-<stamp>.
Run by system/system-dram.sh (a `dram apply` hook). Root, unless --dry-run.

  --theme NAME   letterpress (default) | catppuccin (the old theme)
  --dry-run      print what would change; touch nothing
  -h, --help     this text

exit: 0 ok · 1 not root, no UKIs on the ESP, Secure Boot on without sbctl keys, or a
      step failed · 2 bad usage
see: docs/platforms/arch/boot-chain.md
```

### `decommission.sh`

invoked by: by hand

```
usage: decommission.sh [--plan | --execute [--dry-run] [--delete-age-key]]

Retires THIS host from the dram. --plan (the default) changes nothing: it
prints, numbered, every artefact this host holds or is referenced by and
the exact command that removes each — the copy of its data you keep, the
.sops.yaml recipient, modules/hosts/<host>.nix + hosts/<host>/, the Mac
scripts that name it, the [dram] builder role and the signing key's
custody, the YubiKeys (nothing on them is per host), the UniFi WireGuard
client + DHCP reservation, the GitHub keys, and the local state. While
backups are paused (decisions/0014) a host has no peer; with one, the plan
adds its Borg repo on the peer, its pinned key there and any host whose
backupPeer is this one. Peer-side and Mac-side steps are PRINTED, never run
from here: bin/forget-host.sh <host> does the Mac side. --execute runs only
the local steps a reinstall would undo anyway: stops the user timers,
removes the Home Manager profiles and state, the builder's /srv/dram and
chroot, the plaintext Borg passphrase if one exists. It never touches
~/backups/borg (a peer's data), ~/.ssh, ~/.gnupg (the signing key) or the
disk; the age key goes only with --delete-age-key. Asks for the hostname
typed back and refuses without a terminal. Runs as the host's user; sudo
only for /srv/dram and the chroot.

  --plan             print the plan (default)
  --execute          run the local steps, after the typed hostname
  --dry-run          with --execute: print the commands, change nothing, no prompt
  --delete-age-key   with --execute: also delete ~/.config/sops/age/keys.txt
  -h, --help         this text

exit: 0 ok · 1 refused (no terminal, name mismatch, not a dram host) · 2 bad usage
see: docs/records/handbook/10-teardown.md
```

### `dram-builder-setup.sh`

invoked by: by hand

```
usage: dram-builder-setup.sh [--dry-run] [--refresh] [--migrate-from-rice]

Makes cabin the build host for the [dram] package repo: installs
packages/roles/builder.txt (devtools, diffoscope), creates the clean chroot
/var/lib/archbuild/dram-x86_64 from devtools' own pacman.conf (official
repos only; the chroot must never see [dram], or it would build against
itself), creates the staging dir /srv/dram owned by the builder user, and
PRINTS how to make the signing key as pj (`dram pkgs key --new`; it never
generates a key itself). Root, idempotent.

  --refresh       also `pacman -Syu` the existing chroot root (network-heavy;
                  makechrootpkg -u already updates the working copy per build,
                  so a plain re-run leaves the root alone)
  --migrate-from-rice   the builder was set up under the [rice] name (until
                  2026-10-06): mv /srv/rice to /srv/dram and rename rice.db* /
                  rice.files* inside it to dram.* (signatures stay valid), mv the
                  chroot /var/lib/archbuild/rice-x86_64 to dram-x86_64, add the
                  "pj dram packages" uid to the signing key as the builder user
                  and make it primary, re-export pkgs/dram.asc; prints the
                  commit command. Then the normal steps.
  -n, --dry-run   no root needed; print what would change
  -h, --help      this text

env: DRAM_BUILDER_HOST=<name>   allow a host other than cabin
     DRAM_BUILDER_USER=<user>   default: the sudo caller, else pj

### `dram-snapshot.sh`

invoked by: by hand

```
usage: dram-snapshot.sh <pre DESC | post | ukis | list | rollback N> [--dry-run]

The root half of SteamOS-style safety (decisions/0011), installed by
system/snapshots-setup.sh to /usr/local/lib/dram/dram-snapshot and run by
pacman hooks and `dram rollback --system`:
  pre DESC     snapper "pre" snapshot of / before a pacman transaction
               (system/hooks/00-dram-snap-pre.hook); its number is kept in
               /run/dram-snap.pre for the post half
  post         the matching "post" snapshot (zz-dram-snap-post.hook), then ukis
  ukis         one signed UKI per kept "pre" snapshot (the newest 5), built
               inside that snapshot from ITS kernel and modules, booting it
               read-only with a throwaway overlay (systemd.volatile=overlay);
               stale ones are removed. systemd-boot lists them by themselves.
  list         the snapshots and which have a boot entry
  rollback N   make snapshot N the new root: @ -> @.broken-<stamp>, a
               writable copy of N becomes @, the live UKI is rebuilt inside it;
               reboot to finish. The broken root stays until you delete it.
Replaces snap-pac (no release since 2021: decisions/0013 Community). Root.

  --dry-run     print what would happen (rollback, ukis)
  -h, --help    this text

exit: 0 ok · 1 a step failed or not root · 2 bad usage
see: decisions/0011-disk-boot-secure-boot-snapshots.md
```

### `fido2-enroll.sh`

invoked by: by hand

```
usage: fido2-enroll.sh [--dry-run] [--label LABEL | --wipe LABEL]

lantern's disk (decisions/0019): enrols the one YubiKey plugged in as a
FIDO2 token of the LUKS2 volume install/arch-install.sh made (its FIDO2 PIN + a touch),
beside TPM2 + PIN and the recovery key, so a TPM that refuses (a firmware or Secure Boot
change) is answered by a YubiKey instead of the 48-character recovery key. Run it once
per key, that key alone plugged in. It also keeps the volume in the shape the boot needs
on every run: the TPM2 keyslot at priority `prefer`, libfido2 inside the UKI, and
rd.luks.options=tpm2-device=auto,fido2-device=auto,tries=0,discard. Records which slot
holds which key in /etc/dram/luks-fido2 (a lost key is wiped by its slot number). Does
nothing on a host without LUKS. Root, unless --dry-run.

  -n, --dry-run     print what would change
  --label LABEL     the key's label in keys/ (primary, spare); asked when omitted
  --wipe LABEL      a lost key: wipe its slot (from /etc/dram/luks-fido2; needs no
                    key and no unlock) and forget it
  -h, --help        this text

needs:  cryptsetup with systemd-cryptenroll, libfido2, mkinitcpio and UKIs,
        install/lib/luks.sh; one YubiKey with a FIDO2 PIN; root unless --dry-run
alone:  yes on a LUKS2 volume with a TPM2 slot, with luks.sh beside it in install/lib/
here:   an `ask` hook of `dram apply` on metal hosts (system/apply-hooks.tsv), after
        tpm2-enroll.sh
exit:   0 ok (or nothing to do) · 1 not root, no single key with a FIDO2 PIN, or a step
        failed · 2 bad usage

Required DatabaseRequired, Server = file:///var/lib/dram-repo), creates
/var/lib/dram-repo owned by the user who rsyncs into it, and inserts the
Include above [core] in /etc/pacman.conf once the repo has been synced (a
missing dram.db would make every pacman -Sy fail). Refuses to run without
pkgs/dram.asc (generate the key on cabin first: system/dram-builder-setup.sh

BOTH hosts after any change to the key — a new expiry, an added or revoked
uid: pacman-key --add re-imports the new packets, pacman's keyring keeps the
old ones otherwise. Afterwards: dram update.

                  line to dram.conf in place, drop rice.conf, mv /var/lib/rice-repo
                  to /var/lib/dram-repo and rename rice.db* / rice.files* inside
                  it to dram.* (plain renames; the detached signatures stay
                  valid), then the normal steps and a final pacman -Sy
