### `secureboot-test.sh`

invoked by: by hand

```
usage: secureboot-test.sh --arm | --check | --dry-run

Proves that the firmware enforces Secure Boot for the internal disk, not only that it
reports "enabled": some firmware runs unsigned images anyway (MSI boards until the
"Secure Boot Preset" is set to "Maximum Security": handbook 01 §2; sbctl's quirk
FQ0001, which sbctl infers from the board model and cannot verify).
  --arm     copies systemd's stock, unsigned systemd-bootx64.efi to
            /efi/EFI/dramtest/test.efi, adds a firmware boot entry for it without
            touching BootOrder (efibootmgr --create-only) and sets BootNext to it.
            Then reboot: an enforcing firmware refuses the image (often with a
            message: press Enter) and boots the normal entry instead.
  --check   after that reboot: says which entry booted (BootCurrent), then removes
            the test entry and the file. Exit 0 = refused (enforcing), 1 = the
            unsigned image ran (not enforcing), 2 = not armed.
The removable-media half needs no script: boot an unsigned ISO (the Arch ISO) from
the firmware's boot menu; it must be refused. Run again after a BIOS update, a CMOS
clear or "Load Defaults", which can reset the preset. Root, unless --dry-run.

  --dry-run    print what --arm would do; change nothing
  -h, --help   this text

needs:  efibootmgr, systemd-boot's unsigned stub, an ESP at /efi; root unless --dry-run
alone:  yes on any UEFI host with Secure Boot on
here:   by hand, after secureboot-setup.sh and after any firmware change
exit:   0 ok (--check: enforcing) · 1 a step failed (--check: not enforcing) · 2 bad usage or not armed
see:    docs/security/boot-trust/secure-boot.md, docs/records/handbook/01-install.md §8,
        docs/records/handbook/11-troubleshooting.md
```

### `snapshots-setup.sh`

invoked by: by hand

```
usage: snapshots-setup.sh [--dry-run]

Turns on SteamOS-style snapshots for this host (decisions/0011): snapper
configs `root` (/) and `home` (/home) on the @snapshots / @home_snapshots
subvolumes install/arch-install.sh made, the dram-snapshot helper in
/usr/local/lib/dram/, the pacman hooks that snapshot before and after every
transaction and build a boot entry per snapshot, and the snapper timers.
Idempotent; a `dram apply` role hook (system/apply-hooks.tsv). Skips with a
note on a host without btrfs or without the @snapshots layout (the older
ext4 hosts). Root, unless --dry-run.

  -n, --dry-run   print what would change
  -h, --help      this text

exit: 0 ok (or skipped) · 1 not root or a step failed · 2 bad usage
see: decisions/0011-disk-boot-secure-boot-snapshots.md
```

### `system-dram.sh`

invoked by: by hand

```
usage: system-dram.sh [--dry-run]

sudo-required system ricing, a thin orchestrator of the boot look, in boot order:
1) rEFInd as the themed menu in front of the UKIs, signed (system/apply-refind.sh);
2) the Plymouth splash on the UKIs, the fallback UKIs left verbose
(system/plymouth-setup.sh); 3) the ly greeter in the house palette
(system/apply-ly.sh); 4) collapse the two Hyprland sessions into one. Steps 1-3 are
write-on-change with a single .bak-<stamp>; step 4 is idempotent. 1 and 2 need a UKI
host (install/arch-install.sh) and, with Secure Boot on, sbctl's keys: their hook row
runs after system/secureboot-setup.sh and the LUKS enrolments, which edit the kernel
command line. --dry-run is passed through to 1-3 and skips 4. Root, unless --dry-run.

  --dry-run     no root needed; shows the diffs, changes nothing
  -h, --help    this text

exit: 0 ok · 1 not root or a step failed · 2 bad usage
see: docs/platforms/arch/boot-chain.md
```

### `tpm2-enroll.sh`

invoked by: by hand

```
usage: tpm2-enroll.sh [--dry-run | --reenroll]

Laptop disk unlock (decisions/0011): enrolls the TPM2 into the LUKS2 volume
install/arch-install.sh made, bound to PCR 7 (the Secure Boot state) and a
PIN, adds a recovery key (printed once: put it in Proton Pass before
anything else), tells the initramfs to try the TPM, and rebuilds the UKIs.
The TPM2 keyslot gets priority `prefer`, so the boot asks the TPM before a
plugged-in YubiKey (decisions/0019; install/lib/luks.sh), and rd.luks.options
follows the volume's tokens (tries=0: the recovery prompt never runs out).
The passphrase slot stays: remove it yourself only after the PIN and the
recovery key have both unlocked a reboot. Needs Secure Boot on first (PCR 7
is only meaningful then). Does nothing on a host without LUKS. Root, unless
--dry-run.

  -n, --dry-run   print what would change
  --reenroll      after the TPM refused (PCR 7 changed: firmware, Secure Boot keys)
                  and a YubiKey or the recovery key opened the disk: a new TPM2 slot
                  for the new PCR 7, the old one wiped; unlocks with the one YubiKey
                  plugged in, else asks for the passphrase or recovery key
  -h, --help      this text

needs:  cryptsetup with systemd-cryptenroll, a TPM2, mkinitcpio and UKIs,
        install/lib/luks.sh; root unless --dry-run
alone:  yes on a LUKS2 volume, with luks.sh beside it in install/lib/
here:   an `ask` hook of `dram apply` on metal hosts (system/apply-hooks.tsv), after
        secureboot-setup.sh and before fido2-enroll.sh
exit:   0 ok (or nothing to do) · 1 not root or a step failed · 2 bad usage
see:    docs/security/boot-trust/README.md, docs/security/identity/yubikeys.md,
        decisions/0011-disk-boot-secure-boot-snapshots.md
```

### `u2f-selftest.py`

invoked by: by hand

```
usage: u2f-selftest.py --authfile FILE --user NAME [--service NAME]

Asks pam_u2f, through a real PAM transaction, whether a YubiKey listed in FILE
answers for NAME on this machine. It writes a one-line PAM service (default
dram-u2f-test) with the pam_u2f options of system/pam-u2f.conf, minus nouserok and
with FILE as the authfile, runs pam_authenticate, prints the module's messages
("Please touch the device."), and removes the service again. system/yubikey-setup.sh
runs it before it switches the second factor on, so a host never asks for a key that
cannot answer there (root is locked: a sudo that cannot pass is a lockout). Root.

  --authfile FILE   the candidate pam-u2f mapping file (`user:credential:...`)
  --user NAME       the login the mapping is for
  --service NAME    the PAM service to create and use (default dram-u2f-test)
  -h, --help        this text

needs:  Python 3 (standard library), Linux-PAM, pam-u2f; root
alone:  yes, with system/pam-u2f.conf beside it in system/ (or your own pam_u2f line)
here:   system/yubikey-setup.sh runs it before it switches the second factor on;
        tests/yubikey-t1.sh shows it failing fast without a key
exit:   0 a listed key answered · 1 it did not (no key here, no touch, a wrong
        credential) or not root · 2 bad usage
see:    docs/security/identity/yubikeys.md, decisions/0019-yubikeys.md
```

### `uki-presets.sh`

invoked by: by hand

```
usage: uki-presets.sh [--check | --dry-run]

One UKI per installed kernel on a systemd-boot host (decisions/0011). The installer
writes linux's preset; a kernel installed later — cabin's linux-lts, from
packages/host-cabin.txt — gets mkinitcpio's template instead, which builds an
initramfs in /boot that systemd-boot never shows. For every kernel in
/usr/lib/modules/*/pkgbase whose preset has no default_uki, this writes the UKI
preset (the shape install/arch-install.sh writes for linux), removes that kernel's
/boot initramfs images, runs `mkinitcpio -p <kernel>` and, once the Secure Boot keys
exist, signs the new UKIs and registers them with sbctl (re-signed on every update
from then on). Idempotent: a `dram apply` hook (before secureboot-setup.sh) and
bootstrap phase 5 run it; `dram doctor --boot` names it when a kernel has no UKI. A
host without /efi/EFI/Linux (rEFInd) is left alone. Root, except --check.

  --check      list the kernels without a UKI preset; change nothing (exit 1 if any)
  --dry-run    print what would change
  -h, --help   this text

exit: 0 ok · 1 a step failed, not root, or (--check) a kernel has no UKI preset · 2 bad usage
see: docs/records/handbook/11-troubleshooting.md, docs/platforms/arch/boot-chain.md, install/arch-install.sh
```

### `virt-setup.sh`

invoked by: by hand

```
usage: virt-setup.sh [--dry-run]

virt-manager for the sysadmin role: libvirt answers through its socket (libvirtd.socket
enabled), and the main user is in `libvirt`, so virt-manager manages the system's VMs
without asking for a password (log out and in once after the first run). Its NAT network's
VMs ask the host's dnsmasq for DHCP and DNS on virbr0: /etc/nftables.d/libvirt.nft lets
exactly that in (the forward chain already passes bridge traffic; system/nftables.conf),
checked with `nft -c` before the firewall reloads. VM disks belong on /data/vm.
Idempotent; an `ask` hook of `dram apply` (it touches the firewall). Root, unless --dry-run.

  -n, --dry-run   print what would change
  -h, --help      this text

env: DRAM_USER (default: the sudo caller, else pj)
exit: 0 ok · 1 not root, libvirt missing, or a step failed · 2 bad usage
see: docs/toolchain/development/README.md
```

### `windows-esp-retire.sh`

invoked by: by hand

```
usage: windows-esp-retire.sh [--dry-run]

Takes Windows' boot files off Arch's ESP once Windows boots from its own
(decisions/log.md#d65; install/windows/dram-windows/own-esp.ps1): Windows Setup
had put \EFI\Microsoft on Arch's ESP, so Windows servicing wrote into Arch's boot partition.
Only when Windows' own ESP (FAT label WIN-ESP) holds \EFI\Microsoft\Boot\bootmgfw.efi and a
"Windows Boot Manager" NVRAM entry points at it: archives <ESP>/EFI/Microsoft to
/var/lib/dram/backup/efi-microsoft-<stamp>.tar, removes it, and deletes every other
"Windows Boot Manager" NVRAM entry (the one MSI's firmware re-adds for any ESP holding
bootmgfw.efi, and the old drives'); then runs apply-refind.sh so the Windows tile starts
Windows' own entry. Without WIN-ESP it changes nothing. Idempotent; an `ask` hook of
`dram apply`. Root, unless --dry-run.

  -n, --dry-run   print what would change
  -h, --help      this text

exit: 0 done or nothing to do · 1 not root, a check or a step failed · 2 bad usage
rollback: tar -xf the archive into <ESP>/EFI/, then efibootmgr -c for its entry
see: docs/platforms/windows/boot-guard.md, docs/platforms/arch/boot-chain.md
```

### `wsl-setup.sh`

invoked by: by hand

```
usage: wsl-setup.sh [--dry-run]

The system half of a WSL clone (decisions/0021, docs/platforms/wsl/README.md): what turns
the official
Arch image into a converged host, written from the repo and changed only where it differs.
The wsl pseudo-role's `dram apply` hook (system/apply-hooks.tsv); outside WSL it does
nothing. In order:
  1) /etc/wsl.conf from system/wsl/wsl.conf (hostname, default user, systemd,
     appendWindowsPath=false) and /etc/hostname; a change takes effect once the distro
     has stopped: `wsl.exe --terminate <distro>` from Windows (the last line says so)
  2) the units Microsoft lists as breaking WSL stay masked (networkd, resolved,
     NetworkManager, the tmpfiles units, tmp.mount); the metal units stay off
  3) linger for the login: its user manager (the agent bridge, rootless Podman) runs
     without a terminal open
  4) rootless Podman: subordinate ids for the login, the file capabilities of
     newuidmap/newgidmap (an imported rootfs loses them), / shared (dram-wsl-rshared)
  5) sshd for VSCodium's Open Remote - SSH: 127.0.0.1:2222, keys only, a touch for a
     security key (system/wsl/sshd.conf), the YubiKeys' keys from keys/ssh.pub in
     /etc/ssh/authorized_keys.d/<login> (as system/harden.sh writes them on metal)
  6) a YubiKey attached with usbipd: its hidraw node for wheel (system/wsl/*.rules)
Root, unless --dry-run.

  -n, --dry-run   print what would change
  -h, --help      this text

env: DRAM_USER (default: the sudo caller, else pj), DRAM_HOST (default: /etc/hostname)
exit: 0 ok (or not WSL) · 1 not root, not a WSL host file, or a step failed · 2 bad usage
see: docs/platforms/wsl/README.md, system/wsl/README.md
```

### `yubikey-setup.sh`

invoked by: by hand

```
usage: yubikey-setup.sh [--dry-run | --off]

The YubiKey as the second factor on a desktop host (decisions/0019): writes the
pam_u2f line of system/pam-u2f.conf right after the password line of
/etc/pam.d/sudo, polkit-1 and login (ly, hyprlock and the console include login), and
/etc/dram/u2f_mappings for this host's login from keys/pam-u2f.txt. The second factor
switches on only after a listed key answers a test touch at this machine
(system/u2f-selftest.py), so a host never asks for a key that cannot answer here;
once on, a re-run follows keys/pam-u2f.txt (a revoked key's credential disappears)
without a touch. A mistake here costs sudo, and root is locked. Root, unless --dry-run.

  -n, --dry-run   print what would change
  --off           switch the second factor off on this host (the map loses every
                  line; the PAM lines stay and ask for nothing). Needs no key;
                  without sudo, docs/security/identity/yubikeys.md has the
                  break-glass from the ISO
  -h, --help      this text

env:    DRAM_USER (default: the sudo caller, else pj); tests/yubikey-t0.sh points
        DRAM_PAMD, DRAM_VENDOR_PAMD, DRAM_ETC, DRAM_PAM_U2F_SO and DRAM_U2F_SELFTEST at a
        temp dir (sudo's env_reset never passes them through)
needs:  pam-u2f, libfido2, python3 (for u2f-selftest.py), keys/pam-u2f.txt; root
        unless --dry-run
alone:  yes, with your own credentials in keys/pam-u2f.txt and your own origin in
        system/pam-u2f.conf; keep a root shell open while you test
here:   an `ask` hook of `dram apply` for the desktop role (system/apply-hooks.tsv);
        `dram doctor` ("yubikeys") says when the second factor is off
exit:   0 ok (second factor on, or not yet: nothing listed / no key here) · 1 not root
        or a step failed · 2 bad usage
see:    docs/security/identity/yubikeys.md
```

## `install/`

The installer and the Mac's launchd job.

### `arch-install.sh`

invoked by: by hand

```
usage: arch-install.sh --preset NAME --disk PATH --hostname NAME [options]

Puts Arch on one disk (plus, for the bench preset, a second "work" disk) from the Arch ISO (decisions/0010): GPT with an ESP at
/efi, btrfs with the subvolume layout of decisions/0011 (a data pool on
desktops, LUKS2 on laptops), a minimal base from the pinned mirrors
(install/mirrorlist — nothing here talks to archlinux.org), a UKI booted by
systemd-boot, networking, the user, a copy of this repo at
~/git/dotfiles and the host file with its roles. First boot continues with
install/bootstrap.sh, which runs `dram apply`; Secure Boot, snapshots and
the per-snapshot boot entries come with `dram apply`'s hooks. Run as root from the ISO,
out of a checkout of this repo (USB stick, or git clone from the Mac).

Safety: every disk is listed first and only --disk is touched; a disk that
holds NTFS, BitLocker or a Windows boot manager is refused; you type the
disk's serial number to confirm (or pass it with --yes-wipe).

  --preset NAME         install/presets/NAME.env: desktop | laptop | admin | vm-test
  --disk PATH           the target, ideally /dev/disk/by-id/...
  --hostname NAME       the new host's name (modules/hosts/NAME.nix)
  --roles "A B"         roles for a new host file (asked when missing and the
                        repo has no modules/hosts/NAME.nix)
  --user NAME           the login user (default pj)
  --timezone ZONE       default America/New_York
  --sys-gib N           override the preset's system-pool size (desktop presets)
  --work-disk PATH      a second disk for the work pool (VMs, ML, containers, scratch;
                        the bench preset requires it, decisions/0017); wiped the same way
  --yes-wipe SERIAL     confirm the wipe without the prompt (VM tests)
  --yes-wipe-work SERIAL  the same for --work-disk
  --password-file FILE  the user's password, first line (VM tests); otherwise asked
  --luks-keyfile FILE   LUKS passphrase file (VM tests); otherwise asked
  --sshd                enable sshd on first boot (vm-test does by default)
  --poweroff            power off at the end (VM tests)
  --dry-run             print every command, change nothing
  -h, --help            this text

Every option may also come from the kernel command line as dram.<option>=value
(roles comma-separated), which is how the unattended VM test drives it.

exit: 0 ok · 1 refused or a step failed · 2 bad usage
see: decisions/0010-install-path.md, decisions/0011-disk-boot-secure-boot-snapshots.md
```

### `bootstrap.sh`

invoked by: by hand on a fresh box (`docs/platforms/arch/install.md`)

```
usage: bootstrap.sh [--dry-run] [--yes|-y] [--phase N]

Builds pj's Hyprland dram on a fresh (or existing) Arch box. Interactive and
vendor-aware: detects CPU (AMD/Intel), GPU (NVIDIA/Intel/AMD) and form
factor (laptop/desktop), shows what it found, lets you override, then
installs only the matching package sets and writes vendor-correct early-KMS
modules and kernel parameters. Idempotent: every phase is safe to re-run.
The user layer is applied with the home-manager pinned in flake.lock. Two
safety prompts always ask, even with --yes ("repo not at ~/git/dotfiles -
continue anyway?" and "/nix half-removed - proceed regardless?"); phase 6
(hardening) always asks. Inside WSL (a host file with form = "wsl", the clone of
decisions/0021) only phases 1 and 3 run: Windows owns the kernel, the boot chain,
the firewall and the session, and the clone has no [dram] repo.

  --dry-run     print every action, change nothing
  --yes, -y     accept detection, run phases 1-5 unasked
  --phase N     run one phase only
  -h, --help    this text

exit: 0 ok · 1 a phase failed or was refused · 2 bad usage
see: docs/platforms/arch/install.md
```

### `get-iso.sh`

invoked by: by hand

```
usage: get-iso.sh [DIR]

Downloads the pinned Arch ISO (install/iso.pin) and its signature into DIR
(default ~/vm-bench/iso), then verifies the sha256 AND the release signature
against the pinned key fingerprint, in a throwaway GnuPG home. Prints the
path of the verified ISO. Runs on the Mac or any Linux with curl + gpg; write
it to a USB stick yourself (dd / Disk Utility) after it says OK.

  -h, --help    this text

exit: 0 verified · 1 download, checksum or signature failed · 2 bad usage
see: decisions/0010-install-path.md
```

### `mac-launchd.sh`

invoked by: by hand on the Mac, once

```
usage: mac-launchd.sh [--uninstall | --status]

Installs (or refreshes) the Mac launchd job dev.pj.pull-backups that runs
bin/pull-backups.sh daily at 06:00 and once whenever the job is loaded
(RunAtLoad: at every login, and at this install itself, so running this
script triggers one pull right away). launchd replays a missed
StartCalendarInterval only after sleep, never after a power-off
(launchd.plist(5)), so a Mac that was off at 06:00 pulls at the next login
instead; pull-backups.sh skips a host pulled less than 20 h ago, so the
extra runs cost one ssh probe. Writes
~/Library/LaunchAgents/dev.pj.pull-backups.plist, boots the old job out and
the new one in. Logs land in ~/backups/borg/launchd.{out,err}. Run by hand
on the Mac. --uninstall boots the job out and removes the plist; the pulled
copies under ~/backups/borg/ and the logs stay (docs/records/handbook/10-teardown.md).
--status prints the job's state, run count and last exit code from
`launchctl print` and changes nothing.

  --uninstall   launchctl bootout + rm the plist
  --status      state / runs / last exit code; exit 1 when the job is not loaded
  -h, --help    this text

exit: 0 ok · 1 launchctl failed or (--status) job not loaded · 2 bad usage
see: docs/operations/backups/README.md, docs/platforms/macos/README.md
```

## Aliases and shims

Bash aliases from `modules/shell.nix` (`programs.bash.shellAliases`): interactive shells only — a script or `ssh host <alias>` must spell the command out.

| alias | runs | note |
|---|---|---|
| `grep` | `grep --color=auto` |  |
| `cat` | `bat --paging=never` |  |
| `ls` | `eza --group-directories-first` |  |
| `ll` | `eza -l --git --group-directories-first` |  |
| `la` | `eza -la --git --group-directories-first` |  |
| `tree` | `eza --tree` |  |
| `..` | `cd ..` |  |
| `vpn` | `sudo wg-quick up home` | docs/security/network/vpn.md (UniFi WireGuard client) |
| `vpn-down` | `sudo wg-quick down home` |  |
| `backup` | `borgmatic --verbosity 1` | daily timer does the same; this is the manual run |
| `backup-eva` | `bash ~/git/dotfiles/system/backup-eva.sh` | optional offline copy when eva is plugged in |
| `upgrade` | `dram update --clean` | sysupdate/dram-switch are shims onto `dram` (docs/operations/dram/README.md) |
| `k` | `kubectl` |  |
| `kx` | `kubectx` |  |
| `kn` | `kubens` |  |
| `t` | `talosctl` |  |

Shim scripts (real files in `~/.local/bin`, so they work from anywhere):

| shim | runs | note |
|---|---|---|
| `sysupdate` | `dram update "$@"` | kept for muscle memory and old docs |
| `dram-switch` | `dram switch "$@"` | same; never bare `home-manager switch` |
